clue.text: More crooked and possibly better at being kept in the dark?

definitions.meaning: shady means dishonest, so this is the comparative: more dishonest

definitions.text: possibly better at being kept in the dark
definitions.meaning: a plant or spot that does well out of the sun would be more suited to shade, playfully put as more shady

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether the more dishonest person is also the one better at being kept uninformed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kept in the dark' suggests ignorance; here it is read literally as being in shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Shady is slang for dishonest, and also literally means sheltered from sunlight, giving both comparatives.

clue.text: Hand-me-down: what next in line might use for clothing?

parts.note: the person next in line to inherit is the heir
a loom is the frame on which cloth for clothing is woven

explanation.surface: A question about what the next in line to the throne might wear as a family cast-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Use for clothing' sounds like wearing; it points to the machine that weaves the cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasured family item passed down the generations is a hand-me-down in the grand sense.

clue.text: Men in depots kneaded bread?

indicators.note: in says the men are placed within the reworked letters
kneaded, like dough worked by hand, says the letters of depots are worked into a new order

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the usual abbreviation for soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Soldiers in supply depots are kneading dough for bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kneaded' rearranges the depot letters with 'in' setting the soldiers inside; 'Men' are soldiers below officer rank, not just any males.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorstep is British slang for a very thick slice of bread.

clue.text: Pulling out, seeing tense resistance in challenging surroundings

indicators.note: in, together with surroundings, says one piece sits within the other
surroundings marks the word for challenging as the outer casing around the two letters

parts.note: a challenging task is an exacting one
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A dentist pulling a tooth meets tense resistance in difficult conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ... surroundings' is one container signal split by the word for challenging; 'tense' is a grammar term, not a feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Extracting something is removing it by pulling, as with a tooth.

clue.text: Oil's too much, love!

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means excessive
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Someone tells a darling that they have used far too much oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto, also called attar, is a fragrant oil pressed from rose petals.

clue.text: It's dangerous, worldwide organisation having strongbox

parts.note: the UN, United Nations, is a global body
a safe is a strongbox for valuables

explanation.surface: A global body owning a strongbox is warned that the situation is risky.
explanation.definitionFit: Something risky or hazardous is not safe, the plain opposite sense.

clue.text: Save one's thanks for person serving drinks

parts.note: save in the sense of except is bar, as in all bar one
one is I, and the 's stands for is, giving I then S
ta is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: Someone keeps their thanks for the person who brings the drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save' looks like a verb meaning keep, but it is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: A barista is someone who makes and serves coffee in a café.

clue.text: Strange fellows having first bit of trouble in scrap

parts.note: strange means odd
fellows are men

indicators.note: first bit of points to the opening letter of the word trouble

explanation.surface: Some odd men start a bit of trouble in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' looks like a fight; it is a leftover piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddment is a leftover piece or remnant, a scrap of material.

clue.text: Normal type of flag

definitions.meaning: normal in the sense of usual or typical
a banner or ensign carried on a pole, as by a regiment

explanation.definitionFit: Standard means usual or regular, and a standard is also a ceremonial banner.

clue.text: Reply obtained from letter I posted

indicators.note: obtained from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone's answer comes from a letter they sent.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick, sharp retort, so a kind of reply.

clue.text: No — crazy is the beginning of mind wandering

parts.note: crazy means mad

indicators.note: the beginning of points to the first letter of the word mind

explanation.surface: Someone denies that madness is where a wandering mind starts.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadism is the roaming way of life of people with no fixed home, a noun for wandering.

clue.text: Almost a disaster — the gin ran out

indicators.note: out, as in put out of order, says these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The gin running out at a party was very nearly a catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ran' looks like part of 'ran out'; it is fodder and 'out' alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A near thing is a narrow escape, something that came close to going badly.

clue.text: Screen type that's part of donor's contribution?

definitions.meaning: a kind of flat television display
the pale liquid component of donated blood

explanation.definitionFit: Plasma names both a flat-panel display technology and the liquid fraction of blood.

clue.text: Prince possibly not coming back for this dance

parts.note: Charles is an example of a prince's name

indicators.note: coming back says the word not is read backwards

explanation.surface: A prince is perhaps declining to return for a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The Charleston is a lively 1920s dance named after the city in South Carolina.

clue.text: Smart clothing genius assembled with lout

indicators.note: assembled, as in put together from parts, says these letters are built into a new order

explanation.surface: A genius and a lout put together a smart outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A lounge suit is a man's business suit, the standard smart dress code below black tie.

clue.text: Fast-running water: such a tedious thing

definitions.meaning: a tidal wave surging up a river, as on the Severn

explanation.definitionFit: A bore is a tidal surge in an estuary, and also anything dull or tiresome.

clue.text: Direct tax for part of policeman's job

parts.note: to direct someone is to point them the way
a duty is a tax on goods

explanation.surface: A direct tax is said to be part of what a policeman does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Direct' looks like an adjective with 'tax'; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Point duty is a police officer's job of directing traffic at a junction.

clue.text: Coverings that could make a shy mask?

indicators.note: could make says these letters can be made into something new by rearranging them

explanation.surface: Veils that could serve as a timid person's mask.
explanation.definitionFit: Yashmaks are veils worn by some Muslim women to cover the face in public.

clue.text: Lead quietly, getting over bad back

indicators.note: getting over, in a down clue, puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: p, piano, is the music marking for quiet
lumbago is pain in the lower back

explanation.surface: Someone leads quietly while recovering from back trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting over' sounds like recovery; in a down clue it places P on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumbago is an old name for graphite, the black lead of pencils.

clue.text: Standing and helping to hold book

indicators.note: to hold says the word for helping wraps around the letter for book

parts.note: helping means aiding

explanation.surface: Someone standing by and helping to carry a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Abiding means lasting or enduring, as in long-standing.

clue.text: Inspect cut up explosive device

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to axe something is to cut it
a mine is a buried bomb

explanation.surface: An instruction to check a bomb that has been cut open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut up' reads as one phrase, but 'up' alone is the turnaround signal in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something is to look it over closely.

clue.text: Friend finally cries having left girl

indicators.note: having left says that letter departs from the girl's name

parts.note: Sally is a girl's name

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word cries

explanation.surface: A friend weeps after a girl has walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' picks S, which 'having left' removes from SALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is a supporter or partner, so a friend.

clue.text: Wrapping up love-token, in a place where the match might happen?

definitions.text: a place where the match might happen?

parts.note: boxing up a present is wrapping it
a ring is a token of love, as at an engagement

explanation.surface: Wrapping an engagement ring, at the venue where the match, a marriage, might be made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' suggests a marriage given the ring; it is a boxing bout.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxing ring is the roped square where a bout takes place.

clue.text: Poor ailing animal

indicators.note: poor, as in in a bad way, says these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A sick creature is pitied.
explanation.definitionFit: The nilgai is a large Indian antelope, also called the blue bull.

clue.text: Dig up former partner: strong smell emanating initially

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
hum is British slang for a bad smell

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word emanating

explanation.surface: Someone unearths a former partner, and a foul smell rises.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhume a body is to dig it up from the grave.

clue.text: Scrap fish in sort of pudding

parts.note: to scrap something is to dump it
the ling is a long North Atlantic food fish

explanation.surface: Throw away the fish found in a pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumpling is a ball of dough, served in stews or as a sweet pudding.

clue.text: Geek spotted in diner, dribbling

indicators.note: spotted in says the answer can be seen within the letters of the next words

explanation.surface: A geek is seen in a restaurant, drooling.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerd is an obsessive, socially awkward enthusiast, the same as a geek.

clue.text: One who flies, American's in particular part of airport

indicators.note: in says the letter goes within the airport word

parts.note: the runway is the strip of an airport planes use
A is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A passenger who flies is an American in some part of the airport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flies' suggests air travel; it means flees.
explanation.definitionFit: A runaway is someone who has fled, and to fly can mean to flee.

clue.text: Missing milk? It could be thrown into yon drain!

indicators.note: thrown, as in thrown into disorder, says the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Milk has gone missing, perhaps poured down that drain over there.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-dairy food contains no milk or milk products.

clue.text: Sudden eruption — and, reportedly, what might stifle it?

indicators.note: reportedly says the phrase is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: a tissue held to the nose stifles a sneeze

explanation.surface: A sudden outburst, and a question of what could suppress it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eruption' suggests a volcano; it is a sneeze.
explanation.definitionFit: The written sound of a sneeze, which bursts out suddenly.
